q: The Navier-Stokes equations on a 2D torus have a global attractor 𝒜 of finite Hausdorff dimension. The dimension estimate (Lieb-Thirring inequality approach) gives dim_H(𝒜) ≤ C·G^{2/3} where G is:
opts: The Grashof number (ratio of forcing to viscosity: G = ||f||/ν²)
exp: The Grashof number G = ||f||/(ν²) controls the attractor dimension. The estimate dim_H(𝒜) ≤ C·G^{2/3} (or similar bounds via trace formula) uses the Lieb-Thirring inequality to bound the sum of Lyapunov exponents. This is the best known bound for 2D Navier-Stokes.
